audit_enabled.description: Enable or disable permission auditing. When disabled, no audits are performed, but the service remains running.

log_directory.description: Absolute path to the directory where permission audit logs are stored. Ensure the service user has write permissions.

max_log_file_size.description: Maximum size (in megabytes) per log file before it is rotated.

retained_log_files.description: Number of rotated (compressed) log files to keep.

conn_database.description: Database name to connect to. Should contain the system catalog (e.g., 'postgres').

conn_user.description: Database user for audit operations. Must have sufficient privileges to read pg_catalog tables (e.g., pg_authid, pg_class, pg_namespace, pg_default_acl).

conn_sslmode.description: SSL mode for the connection. Valid values: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca, verify-full.

include_schemas.description: List of schema names to audit. Tables outside these schemas are ignored. Leave empty to audit all schemas.

items.description: Schema name to include in permission audits.

audit_rules.description: Per-table audit rules. Each rule defines whether to enable/disable auditing and the audit mode (e.g., SELECT, ALL) for a specific table.

items.description: Audit rule for a single table.

enabled.description: If false, this rule is commented out and disabled.

audit_mode.description: Permission type to audit. Common options: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, CREATE, USAGE, ALL.

email_notifications.description: Enable email alerts for critical permission changes (e.g., GRANT TO PUBLIC, superuser grants).

email_recipients.description: List of email addresses to notify when an alert is triggered.

webhook_urls.description: List of webhook URLs (e.g., Slack, Teams) to POST audit events to.
